name: The Water Challenge
organizer: WaterAid Canada × The AI Fellowship × SOON × TMU
format_note: The overview speaks of meeting the people beside you on the day; the challenge pages do not name a venue.
theme: Ten problems written by WaterAid Canada staff; each team picks one

tracks.name: Track A · Organizational Capability
tracks.description: Tools for WaterAid Canada's fundraising, finance, partnerships, knowledge, analysis and public engagement. The judges' recurring question: would the team actually use this three months from now?

criteria.label: Mission Impact
criteria.description: Whether the benefit reaches water and sanitation work instead of stopping at the office.

criteria.label: Architectural Soundness
criteria.description: A real system with data moving between real parts, not a prompt in a wrapper.

criteria.label: Feasibility & Adoption
criteria.description: Fits their systems, team size and budget. Highest weight in this track.

criteria.label: Governance & Human-in-the-Loop
criteria.description: Who decides, where a person checks the work, how mistakes get caught.

criteria.label: Economic Durability
criteria.description: Running cost against what it saves.

criteria.label: Craft & Communication
criteria.description: A demo judges can follow and a story that lands in five minutes.

tracks.name: Track B · Field Systems & Service Delivery
tracks.description: Rural water services, explored through a fictional district case. The test: does it still work with patchy phone signal, few technicians and a tight budget?

criteria.label: Mission Impact
criteria.description: More water points working, more of the time. Highest weight in this track.

criteria.label: Architectural Soundness
criteria.description: What happens when the network drops.

criteria.label: Feasibility in Low-Resource Settings
criteria.description: Built for about 80% mobile coverage, few technicians and no data team.

criteria.label: Governance & Human-in-the-Loop
criteria.description: Supports local staff and community committees rather than replacing them.

criteria.label: Economic Durability
criteria.description: Cost per water point per year, and who pays when pilot money ends.

criteria.label: Craft & Communication
criteria.description: A demo judges can follow and a story that lands in five minutes.

tracks.name: Track C · Systems Blueprint
tracks.description: The whole Canadian organization redesigned around AI, judged as a plan plus one component that actually works.

criteria.label: Mission Impact
criteria.description: How much more the organization can do without hiring more.

criteria.label: Architectural Soundness
criteria.description: One joined-up design, not a list of tools. Highest weight in this track.

criteria.label: Feasibility
criteria.description: Where to start and what comes next. Lowest weight on purpose: think big.

criteria.label: Governance & Human-in-the-Loop
criteria.description: Which decisions stay with people, and why.

criteria.label: Economic Durability
criteria.description: Build cost, running cost, and what a charity board would accept.

criteria.label: Craft & Communication
criteria.description: Whether a CEO without technical background could follow it.

challenges.title: Donation Reconciliation Assistant
challenges.summary: Match donation records across payment, finance and bank systems, investigate the differences and draft reconciliation summaries for staff review.
deliverables: Working demo on synthetic transactions with an answer key
Data-flow diagram, review screen and a sample summary
Matching accuracy, unresolved items and review effort
Costs, volume assumptions and break-even point
Five-minute presentation of the use and its limits

challenges.title: Grant and Foundation Prospecting
challenges.summary: Spot new funding opportunities, score their fit with WaterAid Canada's priorities and flag deadlines.
deliverables: Working demo on public funding information
Explicit fit criteria and a ranked list with source-linked notes
Staff feedback method, source-update plan and running costs
Five-minute presentation of the quality and limits of the recommendations

challenges.title: Intelligent Reporting and Dashboard Narratives
challenges.summary: Draft plain-language explanations of fundraising, donor and operating data for staff, leadership and the board.
deliverables: Drafts for staff, leadership and board audiences
Visible links from key statements to source data and calculations
Examples of handling uncertainty and misleading trends
Cost estimate and a five-minute presentation of the review workflow

challenges.title: Personalised Stewardship from CRM
challenges.summary: Surface relevant donor history and suggest the next step, so a small fundraising team can keep personal relationships at scale.
deliverables: Demo on synthetic donor records with sample drafts
Review workflow showing sources, preferences and follow-up tasks
Privacy approach and a cost estimate that includes staff review
Five-minute presentation of the benefit and limits

challenges.title: Due Diligence Agent for Ethical Partnerships
challenges.summary: Research prospective partners from public sources, present the evidence clearly and raise questions for a human reviewer.
deliverables: Demo across cases of varying evidence quality
Sample assessment file linking findings to sources and criteria
Review workflow, uncertainty approach and cost estimate
Five-minute presentation of what the tool can and cannot establish

challenges.title: Proposal and Grant Compliance Assistant
challenges.summary: Help staff meet funder requirements, strengthen proposal drafts and track obligations over the life of a grant.
deliverables: Working demo for proposal support, grant management or a defined link between them
Source-linked critique, obligation summary, schedule or compliance dashboard
Staff review, test results and cost assumptions
Five-minute presentation of the chosen scope and limits

challenges.title: Executive Intelligence and Thought Leadership Dashboard
challenges.summary: Produce a weekly briefing that ties outside developments to the organization's strategic and communications priorities.
deliverables: A complete weekly briefing
Source and prioritization criteria with included and excluded examples
Sample communications drafts, a review process and costs
Five-minute presentation of the intended reader and decisions

challenges.title: Measuring Influence
challenges.summary: Track how policy conversations change, find openings, and assess the organization's contribution within collective efforts.
deliverables: Demo on a defined historical or current policy question
Sourced timeline, framing analysis or map of public actors
Method, alternative explanations and limitations
Forward-looking recommendation, cost estimate and five-minute presentation

challenges.title: Kijana District: Rural Water Security
challenges.summary: Keep rural water services running in a fictional district, working through local institutions and community decision-making.
deliverables: Working demo or simulation on the fictional scenario
System map of users, responsibilities, data and links to existing functions
Connectivity, equity, maintenance and financing approaches with costs
Five-minute presentation of likely uses and what needs field validation

challenges.title: Reimagining an AI-Enabled WaterAid Canada
challenges.summary: A practical five-to-ten-year vision of AI across the organization, with one component demonstrated.
deliverables: Blueprint of functions, shared capabilities and human responsibilities
Phased roadmap with dependencies, pilot criteria and investment assumptions
One working component showing the user benefit
Five-minute presentation leadership can assess without specialist knowledge

timeline.what: Teams introduced; teammates meet to review the ten briefs
Each team submits its chosen challenge
Event day. Team Brief editable until 08:30 Toronto time

criteria.label: Mission Impact
criteria.description: Weighted 20–30% depending on the track.

criteria.label: Architectural Soundness
criteria.description: Weighted 15–30%.

criteria.label: Feasibility
criteria.description: Weighted 10–25%; named Feasibility & Adoption in Track A and Feasibility in Low-Resource Settings in Track B.

criteria.label: Governance & Human-in-the-Loop
criteria.description: Weighted 15% in every track.

criteria.label: Economic Durability
criteria.description: Weighted 10–15%.

criteria.label: Craft & Communication
criteria.description: Weighted 5% in every track.

judging.judge_profile_summary: The organizer says promising work will be reviewed by the WaterAid staff responsible for that area of work and its future direction.
judging.notes: The six judging areas are the same for every track; each track weights them differently (see tracks). Presentation polish is worth 5% everywhere.

submission_requirements: One challenge per team, chosen from the ten briefs by Monday, October 12; several teams may take the same brief
Team Brief on the challenge page, editable until 08:30 Toronto time on October 17
Per-challenge deliverables listed in each brief; every brief ends with a five-minute presentation
A finished system is not expected: a prototype, a tested assumption or a new approach counts

guide.summary: A one-day build for a real charity. Judges are asking whether WaterAid Canada could adopt the result, so feasibility, oversight and cost carry as much weight as the demo.
guide.before_the_event: Teams meet before the day to read all ten briefs and agree on one. Research, questions for the WaterAid mentor and the Team Brief can be prepared in advance.

rules.rule: Each track weights the same six criteria differently.
rules.effect: Read your track's weights first: Track A rewards adoption (25%), Track B mission impact (30%), Track C architecture (30%).

rules.rule: Craft & Communication is worth 5% in every track.
rules.effect: Spend the day on the system, the review step and the cost case, not on slides.

rules.rule: Governance & Human-in-the-Loop is 15% in every track.
rules.effect: Show where a person reviews the output and how errors are caught, inside the demo.

rules.rule: Every brief asks for costs and limits.
rules.effect: Bring a running-cost estimate and say plainly what the tool cannot do.

rules.rule: Track B assumes patchy connectivity and few technicians.
rules.effect: Design for offline and low-skill use from the start.

rules.rule: A finished system is not expected.
rules.effect: A working slice plus tested assumptions beats a broad, untested mock-up.

ask_organizers: Is code written before the day allowed, or only research and planning?
Which sample or synthetic data will be provided on the day?
How long is each team's presentation slot, and who is in the room?
guide.harness_note: Run recon, patterns, angles, the judge gate and the demo script before the day. Leave architecture and building for the event unless the organizers confirm pre-written code is allowed.

sources.note: Date, the three tracks, ten challenges, team and choice timeline, what a good result looks like.
Six judging criteria and their weights per track.
The ten briefs: summaries, difficulty and deliverables.

curator_notes: Paraphrased from the organizer's challenge site. Team names and which team chose which brief are left out on purpose. The first event of the nonprofit-challenge kind in the corpus, so there are no same-kind winners to learn from yet.
